body.statement: On the cyclic chart \(\det K_0\ne0\), suppose every mean and covariance coordinate of \(\widehat z\) differs from its population counterpart by at most \(\epsilon\) in Euclidean or operator norm, respectively. If \(\epsilon\le\min\{a_0/4,1/c_M,\kappa/(2c_K)\}\), then \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is defined and \(\lVert\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V\rVert\le c_V\epsilon\). If in addition \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\), then \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) remains stable and off the principal-logarithm cut, its Stein operator is invertible, and every coordinate of the full plug-in \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) is defined. If \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\), then \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\succ0\) and \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}\succ0\), so every dynamical, logarithm, Stein, and covariance-positivity admissibility filter is preserved. Quantitatively, \(\lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert\le c_T\epsilon\) and \(\lVert\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}-E_V\rVert\le c_E\epsilon\), and the principal logarithm, equilibrium, and initial-mean coordinates obey linear bounds determined by their resolvent, \(\lVert(I_p-V)^{-1}\rVert\), and the moment error. These domain conclusions concern the reconstruction from perturbed moments; they do not assert the exact population raw equalities for \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\).
body.justification: The rational chart gives a usable estimator on noisy empirical moments without requiring exact sample spectra or exact probe-Gram identities.
body.gap: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 gives local sensitivity of a loss minimizer, while KoltchinskiiLounici2017 controls spectral projectors; neither supplies a gap-free rational Krylov bound propagated through Stein and matrix-logarithm recovery for common-noise snapshots.
body.consumer: The \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer receives observable conditioning diagnostics and abstention margins for stable generator recovery.
body.proof_tex:
Use operator norm for ordinary matrices and the Frobenius-induced operator norm for linear maps on \(\mathbb S^p\).  Write a hat for a perturbed quantity and \(\Delta A=\widehat A-A\).  The coordinatewise perturbation hypothesis gives
\[
 \lVert\Delta H_j\rVert\le2\epsilon,
 \qquad
 \lVert\Delta d_j\rVert\le2\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon\le a_0/4\), then for every unit vector \(u\) and \(i\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\widehat H_i u
 \ge u^{\mathsf T}H_i u-\lVert\Delta H_i\rVert
 \ge a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2.
\]
Thus \(\widehat H_i\) is invertible and
\[
 \lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert\le\frac2{a_0}.
\]
The identity \(\widehat H_i^{-1}-H_i^{-1}=-\widehat H_i^{-1}(\Delta H_i)H_i^{-1}\), together with the definition of \(B_{\mathrm{norm}}\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat M_i-M_i\rVert
 &\le \lVert\Delta H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
 +\lVert H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
   \lVert\Delta H_i\rVert\lVert H_i^{-1}\rVert\\
 &\le\left(\frac4{a_0}+\frac{4B_{\mathrm{norm}}}{a_0^2}\right)\epsilon
 =c_M\epsilon,
 \qquad i\in\{0,1\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
When also \(c_M\epsilon\le1\), the definition of \(L_M\) implies
\[
 \max\{\lVert M_i\rVert,\lVert\widehat M_i\rVert\}\le L_M.
\]
For \(j\ge1\), the telescoping identity
\[
 \widehat M_i^j-M_i^j
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{j-1}\widehat M_i^\ell
  (\widehat M_i-M_i)M_i^{j-1-\ell}
\]
therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat M_i^j\widehat d_i-M_i^jd_i\rVert
 &\le \lVert\widehat M_i^j\rVert\lVert\Delta d_i\rVert
 +\lVert\widehat M_i^j-M_i^j\rVert\lVert d_i\rVert\\
 &\le\left(2L_M^j+jL_M^{j-1}c_MD_{\mathrm{norm}}\right)\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(j=0\), the same inequality holds with its second summand set to zero.  Bounding the operator norm of a matrix by its Frobenius norm, column by column, and using the definition of \(c_K\), we obtain simultaneously
\[
 \lVert\widehat K_i-K_i\rVert\le c_K\epsilon,
 \qquad i\in\{0,1\}.
\]

On the population cyclic chart, \(K_1=VK_0\) by \(\text{thm:snapshot-frontier}\).  If \(c_K\epsilon\le\kappa/2\), the variational definition of the smallest singular value gives
\[
 \sigma_{\min}(\widehat K_0)
 \ge\sigma_{\min}(K_0)-\lVert\widehat K_0-K_0\rVert
 \ge\kappa/2.
\]
Hence \(\widehat K_0^{-1}\) exists and \(\lVert\widehat K_0^{-1}\rVert\le2/\kappa\).  Using \(K_1=VK_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V
 &=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}-V\widehat K_0\widehat K_0^{-1}\\
 &=(\Delta K_1-V\Delta K_0)\widehat K_0^{-1},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and consequently
\[
 \lVert\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V\rVert
 \le\frac{2c_K(1+\lVert V\rVert)}{\kappa}\epsilon
 =c_V\epsilon.
\]
This proves the first assertion under the first three terms in its stated radius.

Now suppose \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\), and abbreviate \(\widehat W=\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\).  The definition of \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) and the preceding inequality imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat W-V\rVert<c_V\epsilon
 <\min\left\{1,\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}}{2},
                    \frac{\delta_{\log}}2\right\}.
\]
By the definitions of \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}\) and \(\delta_{\log}\), it follows that \(\rho(\widehat W)<1\) and \(\operatorname{spec}(\widehat W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\).  Thus the stable transition and principal-logarithm coordinates are defined.

For every \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), expansion of the two congruences gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)(A)
 &=-(\widehat W-V)A\widehat W^{\mathsf T}
   -VA(\widehat W-V)^{\mathsf T},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert(\lVert\widehat W\rVert+\lVert V\rVert)
 \le c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\epsilon
 <\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}}{2}.
\]
The last inequality is exactly the final term in \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\).  Since \(\lVert\mathcal L_V^{-1}\rVert_{F\to F}=\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}\), factorization as
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat W}
 =\mathcal L_V\left[I+\mathcal L_V^{-1}
 (\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)\right]
\]
and the convergent geometric series for the bracketed inverse show that \(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}\) is invertible and
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}^{-1}\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}.
\]
Thus every operation in \(\theta(\widehat W,\widehat z)\) is defined: stability also implies \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(\widehat W)\), so \(I_p-\widehat W\) is invertible.

Subtracting the population and perturbed Stein equations gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat W}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V)
 =\Delta H_0-(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)T_V.
\]
Because \(\lVert\Delta H_0\rVert_F\le2\sqrt p\,\epsilon\), the preceding two bounds and the frozen definition of \(c_T\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 &\le\lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert_F\\
 &\le2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}
 \left[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F\right]\epsilon\\
 &=c_T\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(E_V=C_0-T_V\) and \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat C_0-\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}-E_V\rVert
 \le\lVert\Delta C_0\rVert+
      \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 \le(1+c_T)\epsilon=c_E\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\), then the two positivity terms in the definition of \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) and the variational characterization of the least eigenvalue yield
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}})
 \ge t_{\min}-c_T\epsilon>t_{\min}/2>0,
\]
and
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}})
 \ge e_{\min}-c_E\epsilon>e_{\min}/2>0.
\]
Thus all covariance-positivity filters are preserved.

We finally supply the asserted linear bounds for the remaining coordinates.  The closed operator-norm ball of radius \(\delta_{\log}/2\) about \(V\) is a compact subset of the principal-logarithm domain.  On this ball the Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the logarithm has the resolvent representation
\[
 D\operatorname{Log}_U[A]
 =\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma
   \log\zeta\,(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}A(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}\,d\zeta,
\]
where a finite union of contours \(\Gamma\) in the slit plane can be chosen uniformly around the spectra in the compact ball.  Hence
\[
 L_{\log}:=\frac{\operatorname{length}(\Gamma)}{2\pi}
 \max_{\zeta\in\Gamma}|\log\zeta|
 \sup_U\sup_{\zeta\in\Gamma}
 \lVert(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}\rVert^2<\infty.
\]
Integrating the derivative along the line segment from \(V\) to \(\widehat W\), which remains in the ball, gives
\[
 \lVert h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(\widehat W)
       -h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(V)\rVert
 \le h^{-1}L_{\log}c_V\epsilon.
\]

Let \(\eta=\lVert(I_p-V)^{-1}\rVert\).  The distance in operator norm from \(I_p-V\) to a singular matrix is \(\sigma_{\min}(I_p-V)=\eta^{-1}\): the lower bound follows from \(\lVert Ax\rVert\ge\sigma_{\min}(A)\lVert x\rVert\), and a rank-one perturbation built from left and right singular vectors attains equality.  Matrices \(U\) with \(I_p-U\) singular satisfy \(\rho(U)\ge1\), so
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{stab}}\le\eta^{-1}.
\]
The reconstruction radius consequently gives
\[
 \eta\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert<\frac12,
 \qquad
 \lVert(I_p-\widehat W)^{-1}\rVert\le2\eta,
\]
where the second inequality follows by factoring \(I_p-\widehat W=(I_p-V)[I_p-(I_p-V)^{-1}(\widehat W-V)]\) and summing the geometric inverse series.

Let \(x^\star=(I_p-V)^{-1}(m_1-Vm_0)\) and let \(\widehat x^\star\) be its perturbed counterpart.  Subtracting the two equilibrium equations gives
\[
 (I_p-\widehat W)(\widehat x^\star-x^\star)
 =\Delta m_1-\widehat W\Delta m_0
   +(\widehat W-V)(x^\star-m_0).
\]
Since \(\lVert\widehat W\rVert\le\lVert V\rVert+1\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat x^\star-x^\star\rVert
 \le2\eta\left[2+\lVert V\rVert
 +c_V(\lVert m_0\rVert+\lVert x^\star\rVert)\right]\epsilon.
\]
Finally, the last coordinate in \(\text{def:parameter-map}\) is the observed initial mean, so
\[
 \lVert\widehat\mu_0-\mu_0\rVert
 =\lVert\widehat m_0-m_0\rVert\le\epsilon.
\]
Together with the transition, Stein, and noise bounds, these estimates establish every asserted coordinatewise conclusion.  The exact raw equations entered only at the population moment vector through \(K_1=VK_0\); no equality of empirical spectra, probe Gram matrices, or empirical raw residuals was assumed.  Therefore the conclusions concern the well-defined reconstruction from perturbed moments and do not claim that \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) obeys the exact population raw equations.
